purpose: Register WPPO's performance capabilities with the WordPress 7.0 Abilities API for AI assistant and cross-plugin discoverability.
riskRationale: New feature with backward-compatibility guards; no existing functionality is modified. The main risk is inaccurate capability reporting (all execute callbacks return true regardless of feature state).

text: Good structural implementation following plugin conventions (namespace, class_exists guard, constructor hooks). The code is clean and properly guards against older WP versions. However, all six execute callbacks unconditionally return true without checking whether the corresponding feature is actually enabled, which undermines the Abilities API's purpose of runtime capability discovery. Additionally, there are minor naming and documentation inconsistencies.

reasoning: Execute callbacks always return true regardless of whether the feature (cache, image optimization, etc.) is actually enabled in plugin settings. This defeats the purpose of the Abilities API and provides misleading capability data to consumers.

message: Proper backward-compatibility guard: the method checks function_exists('wp_register_ability_category') before calling it, ensuring graceful degradation on pre-7.0 WordPress installations.
Same guard pattern for wp_register_ability — clean, consistent, and safe.
Follows the existing project convention for require_once placement in the includes() method.
Instantiation placed alongside other class instantiations in setup_hooks(), consistent with Metabox, Cron, and Asset_Manager patterns.

All six execute callbacks (can_cache_management, can_image_optimization, can_css_minification, can_js_optimization, can_database_cleanup, can_redis_object_cache) unconditionally return true without checking whether the feature is actually enabled in plugin settings. This defeats the Abilities API's purpose of runtime capability discovery — consumers will be told the plugin 'can' do all six things even when all features are disabled.
suggestion: Read plugin options inside each execute callback to return true only when the corresponding feature is enabled. For example, can_cache_management should check if $options['cache']['enableCache'] is set; can_css_minification should check $options['file_optimisation']['minifyCSS']; can_redis_object_cache should check if Redis is configured and connected, etc.

message: Naming inconsistency: ability IDs use 'image-optimization' and 'js-optimization' (American -ize spelling) while the plugin name, namespace, and related identifiers all consistently use British 'optimisation' (e.g., performance-optimisation).
suggestion: Consolidate all ability IDs to use 'optimisation' for consistency: change 'image-optimization' to 'image-optimisation' and 'js-optimization' to 'js-optimisation'.
